name: Tealish
lede: Tealish is a brighter, slightly bluer-green cousin of teal, named the informal way English makes color words: add "-ish" and let the crowd agree.

sections.title: A suffix, not a source
sections.body: The xkcd color survey of 2010 recorded Tealish as a crowd name; our data has no earlier or more formal source for it [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[keppel]], [[jungle-green]], [[light-sea-green]] and [[tiffany-blue]], at 3.5, 4.8, 5, 4.8, 4.8 and 5.2 ΔE [2]. In printed English the word itself peaks in the 2010s, tracking the survey that popularized it [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in exactly 1 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, rarer than 86 percent of the named colors we track [4]. That single match is not evidence the color existed earlier; a 2010 crowd name can still land, by chance, on an old painting's hue [4]. It sits in the [[green]] family, close to [[aqua]] rather than to any pure blue [3].
